meta.title: MOS – The operating system for your home server
meta.description: MOS is an operating system for home servers and homelabs based on Devuan. You manage pools, shares, Docker, LXC and VMs from one web interface. Open source and free of telemetry.
meta.ogDescription: Pools, shares, Docker, LXC and VMs in one web interface. Based on Devuan, open source, no telemetry.

hero.title: MOS – the operating system for your home server
hero.lead: MOS manages disks, pools, Docker, LXC and VMs from one web interface. It is based on Devuan, runs without telemetry and is open source.
hero.screenshot.alt: The MOS dashboard showing system info, network traffic, pools and disks
features.title: One interface for the whole server
features.storage.title: Storage
features.storage.text: Create pools and filesystems, manage SMB and NFS shares, set permissions and attributes.
features.containers.title: Containers and VMs
features.containers.text: Docker with images, containers, logs, networks, volumes and Compose. LXC with snapshots and backups. VMs with CPU and RAM allocation, GPU and USB passthrough and snapshots.
features.system.title: System and access
features.system.text: CPU, RAM, disks, temperatures and network at a glance, a web terminal in the browser, real-time notifications, updates with rollback and users with roles.
features.extend.title: Extend
features.extend.text: Additional features come as plugins. You get apps and templates from the MOS Hub. The REST API and a WebSocket are available for your own tools.

faq.what.title: What is MOS?
faq.what.text: MOS is a lightweight, Devuan‑based operating system for homelabs and small servers. The web UI is a client to the MOS API and covers system monitoring, storage/pools, user management, containers (Docker, LXC) and virtual machines. See the docs: WebUI Overview.
faq.arm64.title: Is there an ARM64 build?
faq.arm64.text: Yes — ARM64 builds are available and are now considered stable.
faq.services.title: Which services and platforms are supported?
faq.services.text: MOS is service‑oriented: available services include Dashboard, Storage/Pools/Shares, Users, Docker service, LXC service, VM service, Web terminal and optional modules like MOS Hub and MOS Notify. Visible functionality depends on which services are enabled. See specific service docs (e.g. Docker, LXC, VM).
faq.install.title: How do I install and operate MOS?
faq.install.text: Download the official release image (see Releases), write it to boot media and boot the target machine. Follow the Quick Start / Installation in the docs to configure networking, create a storage pool, enable services and start your first containers/VMs. The web UI is static; backend/services must be set up accordingly (API, Notify).
faq.security.title: How is access and security handled?
faq.security.text: MOS uses token‑based authentication; for production use run it behind TLS and a reverse proxy. Follow least‑privilege principles, keep system/services updated and monitor logs and notifications. See: System Management.
faq.plugins.title: How do plugins and extensions work?
faq.plugins.text: MOS is modular: plugins can extend the UI and, where applicable, API functionality. Only registered and enabled plugins appear in the UI; installation and management are covered in the documentation. More: MOS Docs.
faq.updates.title: How do I get updates and maintain MOS?
faq.updates.text: Releases and updates are published on the project repositories. Backend and UI may be updated separately; consult the documentation for update and rollback procedures. Release overview: Releases.
faq.opensource.title: Is MOS Open Source?
faq.opensource.text: Yes — MOS and its documentation are open source. See the LICENSE file in the repository for details: LICENSE.
faq.help.title: Where can I find help or contribute?
faq.help.text: Use the GitHub repository for issues and pull requests or consult the docs. The documentation contains Quick Start guides, system management instructions and pointers to community/support channels: MOS Docs.
